Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Hon’ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Mr. Ajeet Kumar Yadav, Advocate for 
the appellant.
Mr. V.S. Rawat, A.G.A. for the State.
The appellant proposes to challenge 
the judgment and order dated 10.12.2025, 
passed in Special Sessions Trial No.14 of 
2020, State Vs. Rajendra Singh @ Rajan 
and Others, by the court of Special 
Sessions Judge, District Chamoli. By it, the 
appellant has been convicted and sentenced
under Sections 5/6 of the Protection of 
Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. It 
is delayed by 43 days. Delay Condonation 
Application, IA No.1 of 2026, has been filed.
Heard.
It is the case of the appellant that he 
belongs to a modest rural background and 
his family members were required to 
arrange financial resources for engaging 
legal counsel and preparing the appeal. In 
that process, delay occurred. 
The delay condonation application is 
not objected to by learned State Counsel. 
Having considered, we are of the view 
that there are good grounds for 
condonation of delay. Accordingly, the 
Delay Condonation Application deserves to 
be allowed.
The delay condonation application is 
allowed. 
The delay in preferring the appeal is  condoned. 
Heard on admission. 
Admit. 
Let call for the LCR. 
Let paper book be prepared and 
provided to learned counsel for the parties, 
as per rule. 
Heard on Bail Application, IA No.2 of 
2026
List this matter on 04.05.2026, for 
hearing on the bail application.
In the meantime, State may file 
objections to the bail application. 
(Siddhartha Sah J.) (Ravindra Maithani J.) 
 31.03.2026
RV

Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Hon’ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Mr. Saurabh Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for 
the appellant in CRLA No.164 of 2026.
2. Mr. V. S. Rawat, learned A.G.A. for the State. 
3. Mr. Bhupendra Singh Koranga, learned counsel 
for the private respondents. 
4. The appellant proposes to file an appeal against 
the judgment and order dated 10.12.2025, passed in 
Special Sessions Trial No.14 of 2020, State vs. Rajendra 
Singh @ Rajan & Others, by the court of learned Special 
Sessions Judge, District Chamoli. By it, the respondent 
no.2 Rajendra Singh @ Rajan has been acquitted under 
Sections 302 and 201 of IPC and respondents, Mangal 
Singh, Smt. Dhanuli Devi, Yogendra Singh, Narendra 
Singh and Virendra Singh Garia (Respondent nos.3 to 7)
have been acquitted of the charges under Sections 302, 
201 and 120-B of IPC.
5. There is a delay of 53 days in filing the present 
appeal. 6. Delay Condonation Application (IA No.01 of 
2026) has been filed by the appellant.
7. The State as well as the private respondents have 
been served with the Delay Condonation Application.
8. Learned counsel for the appellant would submit 
that the appellant is the informant and he did not have 
information on time regarding the acquittal of the private 
respondents, hence delay. 
9. Delay is not objected to by the learned counsel for 
the private respondents and the State counsel. 
10. There are good grounds to condone the delay in 
filing the appeal. The delay in filing the appeal is hereby 
condoned and the Delay Condonation Application (IA 
No.1 of 2026) is allowed.
11. Call for LCR.
12. In the connected appeal, LCR has already been 
called for and it is stated that the paper book is prepared. 
13. List this matter on 30.09.2026 for hearing on 
admission along with connected matters.
14. Meanwhile, paper book be provided to the learned 
counsel for the parties, as per Rules.
(Siddhartha Sah, J.) (Ravindra Maithani, J.) 
 19.08.2026
Akash
